scope: Diagnosis only. No vehicle physics, force coefficient, joint definition, or environment model was changed.

check_1_odometry_reporting_artifact.finding: Confirmed identical 10-sample VRX odometry startup artifact on all 20 full-thrust traces. Samples 0-9 contain a harmonic-decay velocity initialization sequence; sample 10 is the first ordinary sample on every seed.
check_1_odometry_reporting_artifact.assessment: The readable velocity divergence remains a real failure after removing the reporting artifact.
check_1_odometry_reporting_artifact.single_next_fix: Keep the 0.5 s measured warm-up exclusion in VRX summary reporting and retain the raw startup samples in trace artifacts; do not alter vehicle physics to compensate for a publisher initialization artifact.

check_2_graded_thrust.method: Twenty seeds, 2400 samples per seed, identical reset/disturbance/fixed trace and shared actuator lag, with only the first two normalized commands multiplied by 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, or 1.00 before lag and force bounds.

scaling_analysis.interpretation: Position divergence is non-monotonic and already large at 25%, rejecting a single global thrust-gain explanation. Circular yaw divergence, however, scales almost perfectly with command magnitude; the non-linear position error is consistent with an accumulating yaw-channel mismatch rotating subsequent thrust and relative-flow forces.

check_2_graded_thrust.finding: Mixed but diagnostic pattern: not a global force-scale mismatch; evidence localizes first to the commanded yaw response (differential thrust moment or yaw damping/coupling), with position divergence becoming non-linear downstream.
check_2_graded_thrust.single_next_fix: Before changing any broad hydrodynamic coefficient, isolate pure differential-thrust yaw response and align the VRX yaw moment arm/sign and nR/nRR damping mapping to Node. The near-perfect yaw scaling supports this narrower correction; it does not support retuning surge gain or all damping terms together.

check_3_environment_downstream_test.method: For each seed at 30, 60, and 119.95 s, correlate Node-to-VRX position divergence with the preregistered paired environment-response error at the same sample. Pearson and rank correlations were computed for relative and absolute environment-vector error.
check_3_environment_downstream_test.counterexample: At 30 s, seed 20006 has the worst relative environment-vector divergence (628.7%) while belonging to the small-kinematic-divergence end of the checkpoint range. Environment error also falls substantially from 30 to 120 s while kinematic divergence peaks near 60 s. Only the terminal cross-seed slice is strongly positively correlated.
check_3_environment_downstream_test.finding: No consistent positive timestamp-matched relationship exists. Kinematic divergence can amplify environmental differences, especially terminally, but it does not explain the early environment failure; the moving-body environment coupling has an independent defect or mismatch.
check_3_environment_downstream_test.single_next_fix: After the yaw-channel check, audit the moving-frame relative-velocity calculation and NED/ENU force transformation for wind/current using a prescribed body-velocity replay. Do not retune the geometry-derived wind/current coefficients until that transform/sign audit is complete.

ordered_next_action: First isolate and correct the yaw response under pure differential thrust; then repeat the moving-frame environment transform audit. No implementation is authorized by this diagnostic artifact.

approved_followup.summary: Pure yaw sign/moment mapping was confirmed and did not justify coefficient tuning. The moving-frame audit found and replaced the incompatible stock world-axis wind adapter; current signs and transforms were confirmed.
